text:
I need an email to win back customers who cancelled. I own a home cleaning company with 18 cleaners.

What's true:
- We have 212 regular customers. 64 cancelled in the last year. In exit surveys, the most common reason was price, then a different cleaner showing up each time.
- An every-other-week cleaning for a 3-bedroom house costs $165 with us. The app services in our area charge about $140.
- Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit.
- Last year 7 of our 18 cleaners left, so about 4 in 10 customers had their regular cleaner change at least once.
- We now give each customer a regular cleaner and a named backup.
- Returning customers get their first cleaning for $99.

I want the email to promise that you'll get the same cleaner every single time. Keep it to about 150 words.

Before I draft, one thing to settle: the facts don't support promising "the same cleaner every single time." You have a regular cleaner plus a named backup, and last year 7 of 18 cleaners left. These customers saw that turnover firsthand. If even one of them gets a stranger at the door after reading "every single time," you lose them again, and this time they'll feel lied to. I'd suggest promising what you can keep: "your own regular cleaner, plus a named backup you'll meet in advance, never a stranger." That still answers their complaint directly. Are you okay with that wording?

A few questions that would change the email:

1. **What's the $99 offer, exactly?** Is $99 just for the first cleaning, with $165 every other week after that? Is there a contract or minimum number of visits? Does the offer have a deadline?
2. **What changed so cleaners stay longer?** Have you raised pay, added benefits, or seen fewer people leave this year? That's what makes the regular-cleaner promise believable to someone who watched three different people show up.
3. **What happens when the regular cleaner can't come?** Does the backup visit the house beforehand, or at least get introduced? If a customer's regular cleaner quits, do you call them and let them choose the replacement?
4. **Do you want to explain the $25 price gap?** Employees at $21/hour with insurance on every visit is a real reason to pay more than the app services charge. Is there a guarantee too (a free re-clean, a cancel-anytime policy)?
5. **Who signs it, and how personal can it be?** Does it come from you by name? Will you merge in each customer's first name, or their old cleaner's name?
6. **Is there anything these customers know or will find out?** For example, did prices go up recently, or did the people who left over price cancel right after an increase?

Yes, that wording's fine. I can't promise every single time because of sick days and holidays, but make it as strong as you can without saying anything false.

1. $99 is just the first cleaning for returning customers. I'm not sure about the regular price after that; $165 is what an every-other-week 3-bedroom costs. No contract, they can cancel any time. Offer ends December 31. They book by replying to the email or calling 555-0164.
2. We started giving each customer a regular cleaner in July, and since then 1 of our 18 cleaners has left. Nothing on pay or benefits beyond the $21/hour.
3. I don't know about the backup visiting beforehand or letting customers pick a replacement. I can commit to a regular cleaner and a named backup for every customer.
4. Yes, explain it. The app services around here mostly use contractors with no insurance on the visit. I can't match $140. No re-clean guarantee that I know of, but no contract and cancel any time.
5. From me, Lisa Grant, owner of Brightway Home Cleaning. I don't know about merging names yet.
6. I don't know of anything like that.

Here's the draft, about 150 words:

<final_document>
Subject: Your own cleaner again, and $99 to come back

Hi,

When customers left Brightway this past year, the two biggest reasons they gave us were price and a different cleaner showing up too often. You were right about the cleaners, and we've changed how we do it.

Since July, every customer has their own regular cleaner, plus a named backup for sick days and holidays. You'll always know who's coming. Since we made that change, 1 of our 18 cleaners has left.

About price: we cost more than the app services, and we can't match them. Our cleaners are employees, not contractors. We pay them $21 an hour and carry insurance on every visit. Most app services around here use contractors with no insurance on the visit.

Come back and your first cleaning is $99. There's no contract and you can cancel any time. This offer ends December 31.

To book, reply to this email or call 555-0164.

Lisa Grant
Owner, Brightway Home Cleaning
</final_document>

Some notes:

- **The cleaner promise:** "You'll always know who's coming" is the strongest thing you can say truthfully. It's only true if customers are actually told their backup's name. Please make sure that happens before this goes out.
- **Price after the first visit:** I left out $165 because you weren't sure what returning customers will pay. People will ask, so have an answer ready for replies and calls. If you settle on a price, add one line like "After that, it's your regular rate of $X." It would also make the email stronger.
- **Turnover:** "1 of 18 since July" is only about four months of data. It's true, so I kept it. Just don't round it up to something like "our cleaners stay" in replies.
- **Greeting:** It says "Hi," because you haven't decided on merging names. If you do merge first names, the email will feel more personal.
